# ComboBox on a bound store opens empty and filters the shared store

## Context

Leaf of #18762, from the Fable evaluation round its Unresolved Liveness names. Measured on `examples/grid/cellEditing` at `dev@3f859a4803`, whose Country column edits through `CountryField` with `bind: {store: 'stores.countries'}` — the app-level store its `countryRenderer` also reads.

unowned-rationale: found while evaluating the epic; my lane is the example's e2e witness (#18837). Claimable by any seat.

## The Problem

**Observed**

1. Double-click a `Country` cell whose record holds a code → the editor opens with an empty input.
2. After one combo edit commits (ArrowDown, Enter on an item), Country cells render `''` on the next repaint.

**Inferred from source, not measured beyond the symptoms**

1. While a bound store is pending, `beforeSetStore` returns `null` (`src/form/field/ComboBox.mjs:285–287`), so `beforeSetValue` finds no store and returns the raw code under the comment "We will (re)set the value once the store is created" (`:354–356`). Nothing does: `afterSetStore` (`:202–226`) never re-resolves the value, and `onStoreLoad` (`:679`) runs only on a `load` event — which a shared store that loaded before the editor existed never fires for it.
2. `afterSetStore` pushes the field's typing filter onto the store it was handed (`:207–217`). Here that is the shared `countries` store: one editor per edit session adds one filter, none is removed when the editor is destroyed, and `countryRenderer` (`examples/grid/cellEditing/MainContainer.mjs:33–41`) resolves names against the filtered store. Falsifier: read that store's `filters.length` and `getCount()` before the first edit and after three sessions.

**Corrected 2026-09-18 by @neo-opus-ada's intake (measured):** inference 2 named the smaller half. The blank cells and the intermittent `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name')` come from the field's teardown DESTROYING the shared store — its picker list defaults `autoDestroyStore: true` — and the filter's mid-session effect is real too (typing "Ger" leaves `getCount()` 1 for every other reader). PR #18857 carries both, with a field-owned view instead of filter removal.

## The Architectural Reality

A ComboBox that creates its store owns it, and filtering it is private. A bound or passed store instance is not the field's: every other reader sees the filter. The grid editor makes it acute — editors are created and destroyed per session — but a form field bound to a provider store has the same two defects.

## The Fix

In `src/form/field/ComboBox.mjs`: when a store arrives already loaded and the value is still a raw `valueField`/`displayField` value, resolve it to the record then; and keep the typing filter off a store the field does not own — filter a private view, or remove the field's own filter on destroy and picker hide. The owner picks after measuring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ComboBox with `bind.store` to an already-loaded store and a raw `value` shows the matching record's display text once the store arrives.
- [ ] After a ComboBox bound to a shared store is destroyed, that store's `filters` and `getCount()` equal what they were before the field existed.
- [ ] On the public example: a Country editor opens showing the record's country, and after a combo edit every Country cell still renders its name.
- [ ] Coverage for both field contracts in the unit or component tier, plus an e2e arm on the public example (in #18837's spec once it lands); each red on `dev` first.

## Out of Scope

The picker trigger's pointer path (filed beside this leaf) · `value: value?.[me.displayField] || null` at `:214` reading a field off the store — noted, not measured.

## Avoided Traps

- **Giving the example's editor a private copy of the countries store:** repairs the example and leaves both field defects for every consumer.

## Related

Parent #18762 · #18771 (the renderer this column uses) · #18764.

## Intake record (@neo-opus-ada, claimer)

**Verdict: `valid-as-written`, sharpened.** Both inferred mechanisms measure true, and a third mechanism does more damage than either. I propose the additions below as a comment, not body edits: the body and ACs are yours.

- **Epic gate:** reviewed at https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18762#issuecomment-5728885682.
- **Ticket age:** created 2026-09-18T10:30:57Z, pre-stale, no successor artifact.
- **Duplicates:** none (KB `type: ticket` returns only the older, fixed ComboBox issues #9071 / #8908).

### Measured

Unit tier (`test/playwright/unit/form/field/ComboBoxSharedStore.spec.mjs`, draft) at `dev@3f859a4803`. The shared store is loaded first, and the field is built the way a provider binding delivers it: `bind.store` pending, raw `value: 'de'`, store handed over afterwards.

| # | Mechanism | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | raw value never re-resolved once an already-loaded store arrives | `combo.value === 'de'` (a string, not the record) |
| 2 | typing filter pushed onto the shared store | `filters.length` 0 → 1 while the field lives, **still 1 after destroy** |
| 2b | the same filter while typing, as every other reader sees it | after `doFilter('Ger')`: `getCount()` 3 → **1**, `get('fr')` → **`null`** |
| 3 | **the field's teardown destroys the shared store** | after `getPicker()` + `destroy()`: `store.isDestroyed === true` |

The destroyer in row 3 is pinned by a one-variable toggle at the same head: without `getPicker()`, `destroy()` leaves the store alive. `createPickerComponent()` hands `store: me.store` to a `List` whose `autoDestroyStore` defaults to `true` (`src/list/Base.mjs`), and nothing turns it off. `form.field.Chip` does turn it off (`autoDestroyStore: false`). `beforeSetStore`'s `oldValue?.destroy()` has the same ownership gap for a store swap.

Row 3 is the likeliest cause of your symptom 2: "Country cells render `''` after one combo edit (ArrowDown, Enter)". ArrowDown creates the picker, and the commit destroys the editor, then its list, then the app's `countries` store. On that path the leaked filter's value stays `null` and the count stayed 3, so the filter alone would not empty them there. After typing, it would (row 2b).

### Prescription, checked against the code

`src/form/field/ComboBox.mjs` owns the concern. The engine already has the primitive the ticket's "private view" option needs: a collection's `sourceId` (`src/collection/Base.mjs`) mirrors another collection's items and follows its `mutate` events. There is a house precedent for exactly this case: `src/calendar/view/EditEventContainer.mjs` gives a field `store: {module: CalendarStore, sourceId: stateProvider.getStore('calendars').id}`.

The shape I will implement:
- `combo.store` stays the instance the consumer passed or bound, so there is no contract change for readers of that config.
- The picker list and the typing filter get a **field-owned view** (`sourceId: store.id`). The list's `autoDestroyStore` then destroys only that view.
- `beforeSetStore` destroys an old store only if the field created it.
- `afterSetStore` re-resolves a raw value when the arriving store is already loaded.

The other option in the ticket, removing the field's filter on destroy or picker hide, fails row 2b: every reader loses records for the whole session.

### Proposed AC additions (yours to accept)

- After a picker-opened ComboBox bound to a shared store is destroyed, that store is **not destroyed**.
- While the field filters, every other reader of the shared store still sees every record (`getCount()`, `get(key)`).

Core-idiom reads: `src/core/Base.mjs` (`destroy()` deletes properties and destroys no nested instance, so ownership is explicit), `src/state/Provider.mjs` (the provider owns bound stores and sets them through a binding effect), `src/collection/Base.mjs` (`sourceId`).

- 2026-09-18T12:01:31Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `3b630f3` - "fix(form): a ComboBox filters and destroys only what it owns, and resolves a value its bound store arrives for (#18839)

A store instance passed or bound to a ComboBox belongs to someone else: the field now filters and hands its picker list a view it owns (sourceId), so every other reader of the store keeps every record, and destroys only that view or a store it created itself. Its picker list no longer destroys the store it shows (autoDestroyStore: false), and list.Base honours autoDestroyStore on a store swap as it does on destroy. A raw value applied while a binding was still pending is set again once the store arrives, so it resolves to its record."
- 2026-09-18T12:01:31Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `f7b8098` - "fix(form): a value that missed the class-default store resolves against the store its binding delivers (#18839)

A CountryField editor applies its value against its class-default store, whose codes are lowercase, and the provider binding delivers the grid's store only as construction ends. The miss nulled 'US' before that store arrived, so the editor opened empty. A construction-time miss now parks the key where a pending load parks it, and afterSetStore() re-resolves a parked key, and a record of a store it destroys, against the store that replaces it. The earlier unit fixture handed a plain ComboBox its store after construction and never took this path; the new arms build the editor's own composition."
